A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Large Language Bayes work. Their main text, figures, equations, and appendices are readable and matchable. The empty proof in v2 is a confirmed document omission, not an extraction gap.

before.justification: V1 reports original model-generation and posterior-inference experiments on rain, coin, polling, city-temperature, and gold problems in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments, including generated-model success rates, posterior predictions, model weights, and comparisons with flat averaging.

M1.justification: The LLM-generated model distribution, Bayesian averaging, MCMC sampling, and importance-weighted marginal-likelihood approximation remain unchanged. V2 Algorithm 3 moves and summarizes the procedure already documented in v1 Algorithms 8–9.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same rain, three coin-prompt variants, polling, city-temperature, and small/large gold problems. The six in-context examples in Appendix G are also retained.

E2.justification: Flat averaging remains the evaluated comparator across the experiments, and the coin plots retain the same maximum-likelihood reference. No comparison method is added or removed.

E3.justification: The reported settings remain unchanged, including candidate-model budgets, two NUTS chains of 10,000 iterations, data splits, model-validation rules, and importance-weighted estimation settings in Appendix F.

E4.justification: The coin prompt-sensitivity comparison, small/large gold comparison, and Appendix B analyses of individual models, posterior distributions, and model weights are retained. No new ablation, robustness test, or case study appears.

E5.justification: MCMC chain information and posterior uncertainty reporting, including the 90% credible intervals in Figures 5 and 31, remain unchanged. The new checklist introduces no additional statistical analysis or reporting procedure.

E6.justification: The experimental results and plots are retained, including rain predictions of 0.793 versus 0.573 for flat averaging and city-temperature coverage of 44/50 for both methods. The additional gold-data panel in Figure 6 redisplays material already present in Figure 40.

T1.justification: V1 Appendix E.3 provides the full derivation of Theorem 3's joint-divergence result with inexact ELBOs. V2 deletes that derivation, leaving only an empty proof, while retaining the theorem and references to its proof. This removes substantial formal support for the analysis of approximate model weights.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain defining a posterior through an LLM and PPL, approximating it through weighted model averaging, demonstrating sensitivity to user intent, and analyzing inference error. The revised abstract and contribution wording do not materially change these claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 newly suggests that concentration of polling posterior weight on one model may indicate inaccurate inference. Section 6 adds constrained generation as a possible way to avoid invalid models. The Stan normalization limitation is relocated rather than newly introduced.

D1.justification: The new checklist explicitly states that runnable code is not provided because of local-cluster dependencies and non-portable modifications. This adds reproducibility information; it does not establish withdrawal of previously available code. Existing implementation details, prompts, hardware, and timing information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 34 cited works and substantive positioning are retained. The discussion of difficulties applying existing Bayesian model-averaging algorithms moves from related work to Section 3; numbered citations replace author-year citations.

P1.justification: V2 edits explanatory prose, relocates the Bayesian model-averaging discussion and Stan limitation, and brings the experimental algorithm summary into the main text. It adds an acknowledgement and conference checklist, while retaining the overall section and appendix organization.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the two-column main-text layout with a single-column format and extensively resizes and repositions figures and algorithms. Figure 1 is redrawn, Figures 2–4 are rearranged, and Figure 6 becomes a two-by-two display incorporating the existing large-gold data plot.

improvement.justification: V2 offers editorial clarification, a more prominent experimental algorithm summary, and explicit code-availability information. However, it removes the complete Theorem 3 derivation from Appendix E.3 while continuing to cite it. With the method and experimental evidence unchanged, this loss of theoretical verifiability outweighs the limited documentation benefits.
